packageprompt.range.follow.label: Follow the workspace (default)
packageprompt.range.follow.meaning: Use the range the workspace already uses for its own libraries. When it has none yet, smith writes * and says so.
packageprompt.range.any.label: Any version (*)
packageprompt.range.any.meaning: npm uses the library of this workspace whatever its version. You never edit the line when the library changes.
packageprompt.range.current.label: The current version (^{version})
packageprompt.range.current.meaning: npm uses the workspace copy while its version fits, and the registry copy when it does not. Edit the line on a new major version.
packageprompt.library.meaning: {project} will use the code of {library} in this workspace, always its current copy. Nothing is downloaded.
packageprompt.error.none: type at least one package, such as zod or react@19
packageprompt.error.option: {name} is an option, not a package: the box below sets the development dependency
packageprompt.error.nolibrary: There is no library to link: choose a package from the registry, or press Esc.
packageprompt.packages.label: Packages, separated by spaces:
packageprompt.registry.names: Names come from the language's public registry, not from this workspace.
packageprompt.registry.wrong: If one is wrong, smith keeps nothing: fix the name and try again.
packageprompt.command.label: The command that will run:
packageprompt.library.none: No library of this workspace can be linked to {project}: a library must be a lib or a package, in the same language, and must not already depend on {project}.
